plain: To pretend, to put on a false show

webster.text: To invent or imagine; to form an idea or conception of something not real.

more.text: To make a show of; to pretend; to assume a false appearance; to counterfeit.

example.quote: It is not sufficient to feign mere imaginary dangers ; there must be a dreadful reality.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 9, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
